title: Port CodeAssist Icon Manager + integrate as VisualCanvas picker + fix VisualCanvas bugs
description: User wants CodeAssist's Icon Manager ported and used as the FAB-triggered picker in VisualCanvas (not as a separate screen). User can customize icons (rename, variant, tint) — feature parity with CodeAssist. VisualCanvas bugs to fix: (a) no selection scale-up on touch, (b) move X delete button to a bottom action bar instead of inline, (c) allow renaming placed items, (d) persist Canvas items across Canvas↔Source toggle (read XML stubs on entry), (e) make the new XML stub appear in the active tab's code surface on add.

title: Fix unresolved Res.string.edchrome_canvas in EditorChrome.kt:237
description: Build fails with: ide-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/dev/ide/ui/components/EditorChrome.kt:237:47 Unresolved reference 'edchrome_canvas'. The string is defined in all 7 locale strings.xml files (default + en/zh/ar/pt-rBR/ru/in) at line 376. Need to figure out why the generated Compose Resources class doesn't expose it — likely stale build cache, malformed XML, or duplicate/malformed entry elsewhere.
close_reason: Root cause: EditorChrome.kt referenced Res.string.edchrome_canvas at line 237 but was missing the matching top-level import for the generated accessor. Every other edchrome_* used in the file had its import; only edchrome_canvas slipped through. Added the missing import (dev.ide.ui.generated.resources.edchrome_canvas) at line 91, alphabetically placed between edchrome_build_variant and edchrome_command_palette.

title: Visual Canvas Phase 2: drag-to-move + toggle icon next to Save + sync position to XML
description:
Phase 2 of the Visual Canvas editor mode.

User requirements (verbatim):
- Items placed on the canvas must be movable with fingers (long-press + drag).
- The Canvas toggle icon must appear next to the Save (Guardar) button in the toolbar, NOT inside any XML layout file.
- Phase 1 laid the foundation (CanvasItem data class, phone-frame, FAB palette, XML stubs under .platform/canvas/).

This phase adds:
1. **Position field on CanvasItem** — Offset(x, y) initialized at canvas center.
2. **Drag-with-long-press gesture** — switch from Column to Box with absoluteOffset per item; detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress; visual feedback (elevation/scale) while dragging; clamp inside the 280x560 phone-frame.
3. **Canvas toggle icon in EditorTopBar** — new IconButtonCa right after Save (EditorChrome.kt ~line 228); uses CaIcons.grid; click toggles state.editorViewMode to Canvas; string resource in all 7 locale files.
4. **Sync position to XML stub** — on drag end, rewrite the .platform/canvas/<file>.xml with the new coordinates and trigger fileSystemEpoch++.

NOT in this phase (deferred to Phase 3+): resize handles, snap guides, action-chain editor, AI integration, multi-touch, undo/redo for drags.
design: Reference patterns: ide-ui/editor/blocks/BlockDrag.kt uses detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress with onGloballyPositioned + rememberUpdatedState. VisualCanvas.kt currently lays items out in a Column at line 128-145 — switch to a Box with Modifier.absoluteOffset { IntOffset(item.position.x.toInt(), item.position.y.toInt()) } per PlacedCanvasItem. Toolbar integration: add a parameter to EditorTopBar in EditorChrome.kt; place IconButtonCa right after the Save IconButtonCa at line 228; wire the click through a new state.editorViewMode setter.
acceptance_criteria: User can long-press any placed canvas item, drag it to a new location within the phone-frame, release, and the item stays at the new spot. The Canvas toggle icon is visible next to the Save icon in the editor toolbar (both compact and non-compact layouts), and tapping it switches the editor view to Canvas mode. The item's new position is persisted to the corresponding XML stub under .platform/canvas/, and the project file tree refreshes. Dragging is clamped so items cannot leave the phone-frame.
notes:
Phase 2 merged to main (merge commit 1dcd831 on top of feature commit db94600). Local and remote feature branches deleted per user request — all work now lives on main. bd dolt push synced.

REMAINING for full close-out: device verification (long-press drag, toolbar icon, XML routing to res/layout/). Sandbox lacks JDK so cannot verify here.

title: ReTerminal-pattern proot+Alpine shell: device verification
description:
Commit 7125211 ports ReTerminal's MIT-licensed proot+Alpine pattern to the in-IDE terminal. Verified the wiring on disk but no Java/Gradle build was possible in this environment — the actual end-to-end smoke test needs a device:

1. ./gradlew :terminal-proot:assembleRelease && :ide-android:assembleProfile — should pass; the new module compiles ReTerminal's proot fork via NDK/CMake, ~5 min cold build.
2. adb install the APK on an Android 11+ arm64 device (the same kind where the previous Termux-built bootstrap stalled).
3. Tap the toolbar Terminal button. Expected: panel opens with status header 'Extracting Alpine rootfs (~4 MB)…' → 'Reusing extracted Alpine rootfs' (warm) → 'Ready' → TerminalView with prompt 'root@reterm:/ $'.
4. 'uname -a' should print Linux on aarch64 GNU/Linux (Alpine ash, no root, via proot).
5. 'apk add bash' should install bash Alpine.
6. 'ls /sdcard/' should list external storage files (proot bind mount).
7. If the panel still stalls on the user's device, the MainActivity.onOpenTerminal fallback (F-Droid dialog → real TermuxActivity) is intact and still works.

If it stalls, the next debugging step is to check 'adb logcat -s TerminalEngine:* CodeTermux:*' and look at whether init-host.sh is being executed at all. If proot is reaching the args but failing on a specific bind mount, the device's kernel may be missing CONFIG_ANDROID_BINDERFS or similar — the fix would be to make those bind mounts conditional in init-host.sh.
